key_test: 3 (notation, within) x 2 (numerical difference small/large, within) x 2 (task order, between) mixed ANOVA, type III, on per-participant cell-mean RT of correct 'different' responses in the numerical same-different task; term = main effect of numerical difference (Distance)
exclusions: RT<200 or >2500 ms; participant 24 (absent from Order.csv; dropped per Codes.docx); Distraction==1 (filler trials); Distance==0 (same-value pairs); correct==0 (error trials, per the report: 'means of reaction time (RT) of correct responses')

r_script.stat: not run (package missing: ez; also needs car, doBy, reshape2, schoRsch)
r_script.saved_audit_output: the audit's own ANOVA table.png (Analysis Audit output.zip): Distance F(1,29)=42.58, p<.001, MSE=3520.779, petasq .59

agreement: Table and Python agree exactly (F 45.27 vs 45.274; MSE 3574.9 vs 3574.895; p 2.21e-07 vs recalc 2.21e-07). The R script could not be run here; its saved output reports F=42.58, MSE=3520.779. Python reproduces both of its numbers: the script omits the correct-trials filter (all-trials MSE 3520.779 exact) and its F equals the type-2 (n-weighted) test on all trials (42.576); type 3 on all trials gives 42.334.
notes: Anchored on the replication report and the replicators' SPSS output (Results.pdf: NumerDiffere F=45.274, error MS 3574.895, df 29, N 31 = 16+15), not on the audit script, because the script drops error trials nowhere while the report states RT means of correct responses. Mean RT small 804.9 vs large 745.7 ms (report: 807.55 vs 748, small rounding of a different averaging). N.R=32 in the table counts the dropped participant 24; analysed n=31.
